metadata.title: Cryptocurrency Stocks Fall in Premarket Trading as Bitcoin Drops Towards $64,600

content.text:
Shares of cryptocurrency-related companies declined in US premarket trading on Monday as Bitcoin (COIN:BTCUSD) extended its recent losses, trading near its lowest level in three months amid concerns about US interest rates and the regulatory outlook for digital assets.
Bitcoin was trading at approximately $64,600.50, while other major cryptocurrencies also recorded declines, continuing a period of downward pressure across the sector.
The selloff affected companies involved in cryptocurrency investment, trading, mining and digital asset services, with several stocks recording premarket losses exceeding 5%.
Strategy, Coinbase and Other Crypto Stocks Record Declines
Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR), formerly known as MicroStrategy, fell more than 7% in premarket trading.
BitMine (NYSE:BJ) and Galaxy Digital (NASDAQ:GLXY) also declined by more than 7%, reflecting broader weakness among companies with exposure to digital assets.
Circle (NYSE:CRCL) dropped 7.6%, while cryptocurrency exchange operator Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) lost 6.4%.
Trading platform Robinhood (NASDAQ:HOOD) and Bitcoin mining company Hut 8 (NASDAQ:HUT) each recorded declines exceeding 5%.
The movements followed several weeks of falling cryptocurrency prices and reduced investor appetite for assets considered sensitive to changes in financial market conditions.
Federal Reserve Rate Expectations Weigh on Digital Assets
Concerns about further US interest rate increases have contributed to pressure on cryptocurrencies.
Recent inflation data has strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise borrowing costs at its December monetary policy meeting.
Some traders have also begun pricing in the possibility of a larger increase of 50 basis points.
Higher interest rates can reduce demand for speculative investments by increasing the relative attractiveness of interest-bearing assets and tightening financial conditions.
Bitcoin has experienced periods of underperformance during previous Federal Reserve monetary tightening cycles, including in 2022 and 2023.
Uncertainty surrounding the regulatory environment for cryptocurrencies has also contributed to caution among investors.
Nvidia Earnings Add to Broader Market Uncertainty
Investor attention is also focused on the upcoming quarterly results from semiconductor manufacturer Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), scheduled for release this week.
Nvidia shares have declined in recent sessions following reports concerning Chief Executive Jensen Huang's alleged relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of involvement in intelligence activities on behalf of Beijing.
